newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Internet provider set to sign new partners.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Internet provider set to sign new partners.

text.p: Belgian Internet access and service provider Belgium Online (BOL) said on Monday it was finalising negotiations with new partners and would announce details within a few weeks.

"Negotiations are going well," BOL Chairman Paul Huybrechts told a news conference. He said a deal was expected within 14 days but declined to give further details. He also declined to comment on the size of a capital increase.
BOL, launched last October as a secure platform for transactions over the Internet, also presented two new products which are due to be launched next month.
"This will be the new commercial start for Belgium Online," sales and marketing manager Geert De Bock said. "The old BOL does not exist any more, the new BOL starts today," he said.
The EdiConnection product is aimed at the corporate world as a cost-saving Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) solution.
It will allow drastic cost cutting through the standardisation and computerization of the exchange of official documents such as orders and bills.
The translation to EDI formats will no longer be made by company EDI translators but centralised at BOL.
BOL spokesman Salvator Vella said the price-setting for EdiConnection would be announced in April.
The Full Connection product, designed for retail clients, offers 24-hour Internet access at a reduced price after an online registration.
"BOL wants to be a challenger (on the Belgian telecom market), forced to do things better for less money," De Bock said.

Vella said the number of personal Internet subscribers in Belgium was expected to balloon to more than one million by the end of 2001, from 61,000 at the end of 1996 -- an average annual growth of 70 percent.
"Perhaps one million is even underestimated, it is certainly reasonable," Vella said.
Vella said BOL aimed to sign up about a quarter of the expected 6,000 new subscribers per month.

BOL also announced a cooperation deal with the Belgian bank-owned payments company Banksys SA -- a leader in payment cards that use chips to store value -- and the Roularta and De Tijd publishing companies.
BOL will integrate the Proton smart card system into its network. Roularta and De Tijd will deliver the contents which can be bought with the Proton card via the Internet.
